title: Geometrically normal normalization under arbitrary field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $A$ be a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. For a reduced ring $R$, write $Q(R)$ for its localization at all nonzerodivisors [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], where $s$ is a nonzerodivisor if $sr=0$ implies $r=0$. Assume $A$ is geometrically reduced, meaning $A\otimes_k E$ is reduced for every field extension $E/k$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; reduced means having no nonzero nilpotent elements. Let $B\subseteq Q(A)$ be the integral closure of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], that is, the elements satisfying monic polynomials over $A$. Suppose $B$ is finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and geometrically normal over $k$: for every field extension $E/k$, the ring $B\otimes_k E$ is normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then for every field extension $E/k$, the inclusion $A\to B$ induces a canonical injective $E$-algebra homomorphism $B\otimes_k E\to Q(A\otimes_k E)$ whose image is exactly the integral closure of $A\otimes_k E$ in $Q(A\otimes_k E)$. These identifications commute with further extensions of $E$ and with principal localization of $A$. No domain, geometric integrality, perfectness or separability assumption is imposed. The zero algebra is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields, proof: the displayed map A-prime tensor K to B-prime and the paragraph identifying B-prime with A-prime tensor K whenever the latter is normal. The normality argument applies to an arbitrary extension when normality is assumed, not only to separable extensions.

proof.text:
Fix $E/k$ and put $R_E=A\otimes_k E$, $C_E=B\otimes_k E$. Both $A$ (take $E=k$) and $R_E$ are reduced by hypothesis. The map $f_E:A\to R_E$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat]. The inclusion $A\subseteq B\subseteq Q(A)$ is integral by the definition of $B$. Identify $R_E\otimes_A B$ with $C_E$ using
$$((a\otimes e)\otimes b)\longmapsto ab\otimes e,\qquad b\otimes e\longmapsto(1\otimes e)\otimes b.$$
The bilinearity and balancing relations make these ring maps, by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Their composites on the displayed generators are identities: $ab\otimes e$ pulls back to $(1\otimes e)\otimes ab=(a\otimes e)\otimes b$, and $b\otimes e$ maps back to itself.

Apply [lem-per-flat-integral-total-fractions] with reduced rings $A,R_E$, the flat map $f_E$, and the integral intermediate algebra $B$. Geometric normality says exactly that $C_E$ is normal, so the lemma gives an injective $R_E$-algebra map $j_E:C_E\hookrightarrow Q(R_E)$ whose image is the integral closure of $R_E$. In the identification of Step 1 its formula is
$$j_E(b\otimes e)=(1\otimes e)Q(f_E)(b).$$
In particular, if $b=a/s$ in $Q(A)$ with $s$ regular, then
$$j_E(b\otimes e)=\frac{a\otimes e}{s\otimes1}.$$
The lemma states that $f_E$ preserves regular elements, so this denominator is legitimate. The map is an $E$-algebra map since it sends $1\otimes e$ to the structural image of $e$. This proves the asserted canonical identification, not merely an abstract isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C3N (lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields), affine comparison and the normality paragraph; flat total-fraction algebra supplied by the cited lemma.

proof.text: For a tower $k\subseteq E\subseteq F$, the map $R_E\to R_F$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], using the balanced identification $R_E\otimes_E F\cong R_F$, $(a\otimes e)\otimes u\mapsto a\otimes eu$ with inverse $a\otimes u\mapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes u$. Apply [lem-per-flat-integral-total-fractions] with the intermediate algebra equal to $R_E$ itself. It gives preservation of regular elements and hence $Q(R_E)\to Q(R_F)$ with the usual fraction formula. The two maps from $C_E\otimes_E F$ to $Q(R_F)$ agree on $(b\otimes e)\otimes u$: for $b=a/s$ both give $(a\otimes eu)/(s\otimes1)$, by Step 2. Pure tensors generate, so the entire square commutes. This also proves the identity and iterated-tower compatibilities.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, fraction formula in the affine comparison; tower compatibility expanded using flat scalar extension.

proof.text:
We spell out the elementary normality input needed for localization. If $D$ is normal and $t\in D$, then $D_t$ is normal: for a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $D_t$, its contraction $\mathfrak p$ is prime and $t\notin\mathfrak p$ since $t/1$ is a unit. The maps
$$D_{\mathfrak p}\longrightarrow(D_t)_{\mathfrak q},\quad a/u\longmapsto(a/1)/(u/1),\qquad
(D_t)_{\mathfrak q}\longrightarrow D_{\mathfrak p}$$
are inverse by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]: the reverse map sends $a/t^n$ to $a/t^n$, and a denominator $b/t^m\notin\mathfrak q$ has $b\notin\mathfrak p$, so maps to a unit. Both composites fix the original elements and their inverted denominators. The resulting local ring is the normal domain $D_{\mathfrak p}$ by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Thus all prime localizations of $D_t$ are normal domains. Apply this with $D=B$ (normality at $E=k$) and with $D=C_E$ (normality at $E$). The zero localization has no prime ideals and satisfies the same conclusion.

source.place: Tag 037C (lemma-localization-normal-ring), omitted proof expanded using Tag 00CP and Definition 00GV.

proof.text:
For $f\in A$ write $f_E=f\otimes1$. Localizations of reduced rings are reduced: if $(x/f^n)^r=0$, some $f^m x^r=0$, whence $(f^m x)^r=0$, $f^m x=0$, and $x/f^n=0$. Both $A\to A_f$ and $R_E\to(R_E)_{f_E}$ are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. The tensor identifications $A_f\otimes_A B\cong B_f$ and $(R_E)_{f_E}\otimes_{R_E}C_E\cong(C_E)_{f_E}$ send $(a/f^n)\otimes b$ to $ab/f^n$, with inverse $b/f^n\mapsto(1/f^n)\otimes b$; balancing verifies them. Apply [lem-per-flat-integral-total-fractions] to these two flat maps and their integral intermediate algebras $B$ and $C_E$ (integrality of the latter is part of Step 2's cited lemma). Step 4 supplies normality of both localized algebras. It follows that $B_f$ is the normalization of $A_f$ and $(C_E)_{f_E}$ is the normalization of $(R_E)_{f_E}$. Moreover
$$B_f\otimes_k E\cong(C_E)_{f_E},\quad (b/f^n)\otimes e\longmapsto(b\otimes e)/f_E^n,$$
with inverse $(b\otimes e)/f_E^n\mapsto(b/f^n)\otimes e$, extended additively. These formulas respect the fraction and balancing relations by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] and [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property].

source.place: Tags 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), 00CP (localization universal property), 00CX (tensor product); localization comparison by flat total-fraction lemma.

proof.text:
The localization comparison in Step 5 sends $(b/f^n)\otimes e$, with $b=a/s\in B\subseteq Q(A)$, to
$$\frac{(a/1)\otimes e}{((s/1)\otimes1)((f/1)\otimes1)^n}\quad\hbox{in }Q((A_f)\otimes_k E).$$
Localizing $j_E$ first gives the same fraction. All induced maps on total fractions use $x/y\mapsto\bar x/\bar y$: regularity of the images follows from the flat comparison of Step 5. Equality on the pure tensors, and uniqueness of the maps extending to localizations, prove commutativity with principal localization. This applies even when $f$ is a zero divisor: no inverse for $f$ was taken in $Q(A)$, only in the localized rings. If $f=0$ or $A=0$ the relevant tensor algebras and total quotient rings are zero, so the same maps are unique. Neither this argument nor Steps 1--5 select a component, a nonzero element, a separating basis, or a perfect ground field.
